# BlueTusk

> BlueTusk is a PostgreSQL-native platform for .NET covering ADO.NET, EF Core, replication, real-time delivery, extensions, and graph workloads.

Use this index to find the canonical HTML documentation. The complete curated guide set is available at [llms-full.txt](https://bluetusk.io/llms-full.txt).

## Start here

- [BlueTusk overview](https://bluetusk.io/)
- [Quickstart](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/getting-started/quickstart)
- [Installation](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/getting-started/install)
- [Documentation hub](https://bluetusk.io/documentation)
- [Release evidence](https://bluetusk.io/evidence)

## Getting started

- [What is BlueTusk?](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/getting-started/overview): What BlueTusk is, the product families and their status, and where to start.
- [Install BlueTusk](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/getting-started/install): Choose packages and a version, add them to a .NET or npm project, and install the bluetusk tool and templates.
- [BlueTusk 1.1.0 release notes](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/getting-started/release-1-1-0): What 1.1.0 contains, what is new since 1.1.0-rc.1, and how to upgrade.
- [5-minute first app](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/getting-started/quickstart): Start PostgreSQL, create a .NET console app, and run a parameterized query in five minutes.
- [Core concepts](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/getting-started/concepts): The shared vocabulary: data sources, parameters, the type catalogue, logical replication, acknowledgement and checkpoints.
- [Architecture](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/getting-started/architecture): Understand the layers, dependency direction, ownership, and async boundaries.
- [ADO.NET provider](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/getting-started/provider-overview): Use BlueTusk.Data for direct PostgreSQL commands, transactions, batches, COPY and notifications from .NET.

## Provider

- [ADO.NET quick start: a small web API](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/quickstart): Create a table, write rows in a transaction, read them back, and register the data source with dependency injection.
- [ADO.NET concepts](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/concepts): How data sources, connections, commands, protocols, preparation, transactions and pooling work.
- [ADO.NET configuration](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/configuration): Every connection-string keyword and data source option, with types and defaults.
- [ADO.NET troubleshooting](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/troubleshooting): Fix connection, TLS, authentication, pool, timeout, cancellation and type-mapping problems.
- [Authentication](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/authentication): Credentials, password files, TLS certificates, GSSAPI, Kerberos, and SSPI.
- [Cloud identity](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/cloud-identity): AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud identity integration and live-test boundaries.
- [Dependency injection and health checks](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/dependency-injection): Register one long-lived provider data source, consume DbDataSource, and design readiness checks without harming liveness.
- [Connection pooling](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/pooling): Pool sizing, reset behavior, operational signals, and PgBouncer modes.
- [Multi-host connections](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/multi-host): Multi-host routing, failover, target session attributes, and recovery.
- [Batches](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/batches): Execute ordered command batches with PostgreSQL-aware error behavior.
- [COPY](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/copy): Text and binary COPY APIs, typed values, cancellation, and completion.
- [Large objects](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/large-objects): Large-object ownership and streaming behavior.
- [Asynchronous notifications](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/notifications): LISTEN and NOTIFY lifecycle, dispatch, and connection behavior.
- [Sequential readers](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/sequential-readers): Bounded sequential reads for large PostgreSQL values.
- [Schema discovery](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/schema-discovery): Use GetSchema, GetColumnSchema, GetSchemaTable, restrictions, and provider-neutral catalogue metadata.
- [Use PostgreSQL types](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/types): Read and write common, custom, array, JSON, temporal, and extension-defined PostgreSQL values from .NET.
- [PostgreSQL 19 native REPACK](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/repack): Run and monitor PostgreSQL 19 native REPACK safely from .NET.
- [PostgreSQL pipeline mode](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/pipeline-mode): Pipeline groups, protocol Sync boundaries, and ordered failures.
- [Start PostgreSQL replication](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/replication): Open a dedicated replication session, decode pgoutput, and acknowledge only durable transaction progress.

## EF Core

- [EF Core provider](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/ef-core/overview): Set up an EF Core context, query and save data, create migrations, and prepare the provider for production.
- [EF Core quick start](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/ef-core/quickstart): Define a DbContext, create and apply a migration, and query PostgreSQL with LINQ.
- [EF Core concepts](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/ef-core/concepts): How the EF Core provider maps types, batches SaveChanges, handles transactions and builds migrations.
- [EF Core configuration](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/ef-core/configuration): UseBlueTusk overloads, provider options, model-building extensions and scaffolding options.
- [EF Core troubleshooting](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/ef-core/troubleshooting): Fix setup, translation, migration, concurrency and type-mapping problems.

## Real time

- [Choose a real-time product](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/platform): Pick the real-time product you need: Streams, Sync, Live, Control Plane or Continuous Graph.
- [Delivery guarantees in plain language](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/contracts): What each real-time product delivers, when checkpoints move, and what can be duplicated or lost.
- [BlueTusk Streams](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/streams): Turn PostgreSQL changes into complete transactions with bounded storage, durable progress, and safe recovery.
- [Quick start: stream changes from a table](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/streams-quickstart): Prepare PostgreSQL, run a hosted Streams consumer, and process committed transactions with a durable checkpoint.
- [Streams concepts](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/streams-concepts): Transactions, acknowledgement, checkpoints, state stores, spooling, snapshots and redelivery.
- [Streams configuration](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/streams-configuration): Streams options, configuration keys, state stores and limits, with defaults.
- [Troubleshooting Streams](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/streams-troubleshooting): Fix replication slot, publication, privilege, source identity, spool and lease problems.
- [Snapshot and catch-up](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/snapshot-bootstrap): A fenced snapshot-then-stream protocol.
- [Durable relay](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/durable-relay): Storage, backup, groups, retention, and relay fan-out.
- [Checkpoint and lease stores](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/state-stores): State-store contracts and supported persistence behavior.
- [Hosting and observability](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/streams-hosting): Hosted services, health checks, metrics, and operational behavior.
- [BlueTusk Sync](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/sync): Keep PostgreSQL, Redis, OpenSearch, NATS, Kafka, S3, or a webhook current from committed changes.
- [Sync quick start: copy a table to another database](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/sync-quickstart): Copy a PostgreSQL table into another database with Sync and watch inserts, updates and deletes arrive.
- [Sync concepts](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/sync-concepts): Pipelines, whole-transaction apply, idempotency, ordering, checkpoints, rebuilds and retries.
- [Configure Sync](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/sync-configuration): Sync options and every destination option, with defaults.
- [Troubleshoot Sync](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/sync-troubleshooting): Fix destination, duplicate, mapping, lag and permission problems.
- [BlueTusk Live](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/live): Register one authorized query and keep browser or .NET clients updated with bounded, resumable changes.
- [Live quick start: a browser list that updates itself](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/live-quickstart): Register an authorized live query in ASP.NET Core and show updating rows in a browser.
- [Live concepts](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/live-concepts): Registered queries, subscriber scope, re-query and diff, snapshots, resume, batching and transports.
- [Configure BlueTusk Live](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/live-configuration): Live server options, transport settings and browser client options, with defaults.
- [Troubleshoot BlueTusk Live](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/live-troubleshooting): Fix missing updates, authorization, reconnect, resume, limit and proxy problems.
- [Framework guides: Angular, React, Vue and Svelte](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/live-clients): Use Live from Angular, React, Vue, Svelte or plain TypeScript.
- [Control Plane](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/control-plane): Run the dashboard, inspect every product, drill into unhealthy resources, and authorize audited operations.
- [Control Plane quick start](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/control-plane-quickstart): Host the Control Plane API and dashboard, register a component, and query the inventory.
- [Control Plane concepts](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/control-plane-concepts): Inventory, components, health, operations, fleet operations, audit and authorization.
- [Control Plane configuration](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/control-plane-configuration): Control Plane options, endpoints, authorization policies, persistence and Kubernetes settings.
- [Control Plane troubleshooting](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/control-plane-troubleshooting): Fix authorization, missing inventory, stale health, rejected operations and Kubernetes problems.
- [Enable operator actions](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/control-plane-operations): Turn on audited operator actions: pause, resume, rebuild and fleet operations.
- [Real-time operations](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/operations): Runbook for restarts, crashes, failover, WAL growth, restores and rebuilds of the real-time products.
- [Manage deployments with Kubernetes](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/control-plane-kubernetes): Install and use the BlueTusk Kubernetes operator.
- [Keep graph query results current](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/continuous-graph): Keep a bounded SQL/PGQ result current with incremental updates and authoritative repair.

## Extensions

- [Use PostgreSQL extensions](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/extensions/catalog): Choose and configure typed support for PostGIS, pgvector, TimescaleDB, citext, and other extensions.

## Graph

- [Query a PostgreSQL property graph](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/graph/sql-pgq): Define a PostgreSQL property graph, run a safe GRAPH_TABLE query, and inspect or map it from .NET.

## Operations

- [Production checklist](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/operations/production-checklist): Take a BlueTusk application from package selection to a secure, bounded, observable, recoverable, and operator-owned production deployment.
- [Deployment and configuration](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/operations/deployment): Design production topology, security roles, pool capacity, migrations, rolling deployment, and real-time persistence.
- [Diagnostics and observability](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/operations/observability): Metrics, traces, and slow-command events.
- [Troubleshooting](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/operations/troubleshooting): Diagnose connection, TLS, authentication, pool, command, type, EF, replication, and destination failures from the lowest boundary upward.
- [Security review](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/operations/security): Apply secure connection, identity, secret-handling, and diagnostics defaults before production.
- [Performance engineering](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/operations/performance): Measure pool pressure, command paths, multiplexing, allocation, readers, COPY, and real-time throughput with reproducible evidence.
- [Upgrade guide](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/operations/upgrade-guide): Upgrade product families, EF Core, extensions, PostgreSQL, formats, mappings, and rolling deployments with a recoverable plan.
